question.problem:
Consider the function $y={x}^{(2x+1)}.$ Its derivative is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y={x}^{2x+1}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2x+1}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x+1)\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+(2x+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x+(2x+1)\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2x+1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\frac{2x+1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={x}^{2x+1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={x}^{2x+1}(\frac{2x+1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\  & ={x}^{2x+1}(\frac{2x+1}{x}+\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{2x}\cdot x(\frac{2x+1}{x}+\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{2x}(2x+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=2x+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1.$
